families.title: Bayesian and Markov networks
families.intro: Networks against the tools people use for them: Ace 3.0, which compiles a network into an arithmetic circuit, and Merlin 1.7.0's bucket-tree elimination (`-a bte`, and `-t PR` for the partition function), and the other exact network tools: pyAgrum (junction tree), pgmpy (variable elimination), libDAI (junction tree) and TensorInference.jl (tensor network contraction; of its two contraction orders, `treesa` and `greedy`, the faster is shown). On the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks ProbLog, PITA and aspmc ran too. Scallop 0.2.5 ran on the ground program tddlog prints of each network's ProbLog program, every proof kept (`allproofs`), and on the partition function sets on its program of P(e). The exact systems that read Dice programs, Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni and Pluck, ran on the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks, each network as the Dice program of [`scripts/gen_bn.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/gen_bn.py). tddlog reads a network as a ProbLog program, one annotated disjunction per row of a table.

setup: Six jobs on five lab machines (48 physical cores and 743 GB; 36 physical cores and 503 GB; 20 physical cores and 503 GB; 16 physical cores and 251 GB; 16 physical cores and 125 GB), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-21: every baseline of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes, and tddlog alone in a later job for each, on the same machine, in the same lanes, with the same limits and repetitions (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-29) but the UAI networks's in 32 lanes rather than 8, with the same 31 GB a process, the UAI networks asked P(e)'s in 28 lanes rather than 14, with the same 35 GB a process and the final PR set's in 17 lanes rather than 34, with the same 29 GB a process. Each comparison pairs a baseline with tddlog run on the same machine in the same lanes.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. TensorInference.jl's time is its own in the process, warm as Alea.jl's (a second solve of the instance after a warm-up on a small model): without Julia's start, the package's load and their compilation, with its search for a contraction order. Alea.jl's, Pluck's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; Alea.jl's and Roulette's processes' wall times are columns of their own.

tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically as of 2026-10-28 (tididi ca759585, goatd e592d1e). The third literature scan ran a build of 2026-10-30 (tididi df7b84a3, goatd e592d1e). The release's main contains every solver change those builds have. Ace 3.0, Merlin 1.7.0, pyAgrum 3.2.1, pgmpy 1.1.2, libDAI 0.3.2, TensorInference.jl, ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD. Scallop 0.2.5 (668bfb6). Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni and Pluck as on the page of the Dice family's suites.

Every answer of tddlog's, and of each other system, is compared with a reference: the clique tree ([`scripts/bn_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/bn_exact.py)), Ace or Merlin. The largest absolute differences: 1.9e-14 on Ace's networks, 4.9e-11 on the large networks, 9.1e-14 on the 111 UAI networks the clique tree answers (the other five agree with Merlin's six printed digits); no other system answers Grids_15, Grids_16, Grids_17 and Grids_18. For the partition function tddlog's log10 Z agrees with every other exact answer there is: Merlin's, the clique tree's, or a weighted model count of the network. The other network tools' answers against the same references: pyAgrum 248 marginal runs to 3.6e-7 and 337 partition functions to 6.0e-5 in log10; pgmpy 160 marginal runs to 3.6e-7 and 325 partition functions to 6.0e-5 in log10; libDAI 258 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 379 partition functions to 4.4e-4 in log10; TensorInference.jl 392 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 650 partition functions to 4.4e-4 in log10 (the tools print six digits, as Merlin does). A baseline's answer off the reference by more than 1e-9 and either by more than 1e-6 or by more than 1e-3 of it, beyond the last digit either of the two prints, counts as a failure (wrong).

suites.title: Standard suite: programs
suites.about: 71 programs: random graphs, grids, smokers, symmetric smokers, UW-CSE, Cora citation matching, blood types and the Dice paper's programs translated to ProbLog; 300 s a run.

suites.title: Literature suite
suites.about: 319 programs from published evaluations: mnist_sum, pedigree, sickness, noisy-or, mastermind and pdb, each grown on a random structure from a seed, Prob-EC's event calculus over T frames (eventcalc), PSouffle's taint analyses of 15 Android apps (taint), Beame et al.'s safe queries QW and Q9 on a complete domain (liftsep) and paths of two edges in random graphs (rgraph); and the systems' own examples and programs over lists: the ProbLog tutorial's programs and ProbLog's examples, cplint's examples for PITA, PITA's three-sided die, two encodings of the tutorial's grammar, cplint's DNA HMM, left-corner grammar and part-of-speech HMM, and DeepProbLog's handwritten formulas; 300 s a run. ProvSQL ran on the four tuple-independent families, pdb, noisy-or, liftsep and rgraph (the others are recursive or have annotated disjunctions).

suites.title: TPC-H
suites.about: The TPC-H queries as Boolean queries over a tuple-independent database, at scale factors 0.001 to 1, flat and through views (295 instances); 600 s a run.

suites.title: Biomine
suites.about: The probability that each of four genes is connected to Alzheimer disease in the human Biomine network, over the union of the K most probable paths, for ten values of K up to 64; 600 s a run.

setup: Three jobs on two lab machines (36 and 20 physical cores, 503 GB each), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20: every baseline of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes, and tddlog alone in a later job for each, on the same machine, in the same lanes, with the same limits and repetitions (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-29) but the UAI networks's in 32 lanes rather than 8, with the same 31 GB a process, the UAI networks asked P(e)'s in 28 lanes rather than 14, with the same 35 GB a process and the final PR set's in 17 lanes rather than 34, with the same 29 GB a process. Each comparison pairs a baseline with tddlog run on the same machine in the same lanes.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. TensorInference.jl's time is its own in the process, warm as Alea.jl's (a second solve of the instance after a warm-up on a small model): without Julia's start, the package's load and their compilation, with its search for a contraction order. Alea.jl's, Pluck's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; Alea.jl's and Roulette's processes' wall times are columns of their own.

tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically as of 2026-10-22 (tididi c7c0c5d6, goatd e592d1e). The runs on the literature's logic programs ran a build of 2026-10-31 (tididi c5642b97, goatd e592d1e). The runs beside Scallop ran a build of 2026-10-29 (tididi df7b84a3, goatd e592d1e). The runs on the standard suite and the runs beside TensorInference.jl timed warm ran a build of 2026-10-29 (tididi b5d9b21d, goatd e592d1e). The event-calculus programs, the reruns of the literature scan's taint apps and the growth sizes ran a build of 2026-10-25 with twin contraction (tididi b9e5064e, goatd e592d1e) and a recursion over a successor relation grounded level by level, which lacks only the release's sparse route (tididi 9fc0a599). The runs on Bayesian and Markov networks ran a build of 2026-10-28 (tididi ca759585, goatd e592d1e). The runs on the symmetric smokers ran a build of 2026-10-30 (tididi df7b84a3, goatd e592d1e). The release's main contains every solver change those builds have. ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD; ProvSQL 1.13.0 on PostgreSQL 16.4. Scallop 0.2.5 (668bfb6). Ace 3.0, Merlin 1.7.0, pyAgrum 3.2.1, pgmpy 1.1.2, libDAI 0.3.2 and TensorInference.jl. Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni and Pluck as on the page of the Dice family's suites.

Every answer of tddlog's is compared with a reference: ProbLog's (PITA's where ProbLog does not finish), or an exact solver written for the suite ([`scripts/lit_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/lit_exact.py), [`scripts/tpch_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/tpch_exact.py), [`scripts/reliability_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/reliability_exact.py), [`scripts/uwcse_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/uwcse_exact.py), [`scripts/smokers_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/smokers_exact.py)). The largest absolute differences: 3.6e-7 on the standard suite (ProbLog prints eight digits), 5.0e-9 on the literature suite, 4.0e-14 on TPC-H, 3.4e-12 on Biomine; ProvSQL's answers differ from the reference's by at most 2.1e-12 on TPC-H and by at most 8.9e-16 on pdb and noisy-or. The random graphs and grids no exact system finishes agree with estimates from sampled graphs ([`scripts/sample_paths.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/sample_paths.py)). A baseline's answer off the reference by more than 1e-9 and either by more than 1e-6 or by more than 1e-3 of it, beyond the last digit either of the two prints, counts as a failure (wrong).
